worked_solution:
We apply the definition of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =F(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

So, for the piecewise function 

$$
f(t)={\begin{aligned}{e}^{t},\, & t\le 4 \\ 2\, & t>4\end{aligned}
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{4}^{\infty }2\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{t-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{4}^{\infty }2{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{(1-s)t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{4}^{\infty }2{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the improper integral diverges if $s\le 0.$

For $s>0,$ we calculate our Laplace transform as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{(1-s)t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{4}^{\infty }2{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{1-s}{[{e}^{(1-s)t}]}_{0}^{4}+{\int }_{4}^{\infty }2{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4(1-s)}-1}{1-s}+{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{4}^{a}2{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4(1-s)}-1}{1-s}+{lim}_{a\to \infty }{(\frac{-2{e}^{-st}}{s})|}_{4}^{a} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4(1-s)}-1}{1-s}-\frac{2}{s}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }({e}^{-as}-{e}^{-4s}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4(1-s)}-1}{1-s}-\frac{2}{s}\cdot (0-{e}^{-4s}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4(1-s)}-1}{1-s}+\frac{2{e}^{-4s}}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>0.$
